entries.english:
XIIa. Confirmation by Bishop Reinhard of Würzburg for Brombach Monastery concerning tithes at Lengenfeld and Oberbrunn (Schafhof). 1180.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity and its inseparable unity. I, Reinhard, by the grace of God Bishop of the Holy See of Würzburg, have been called by divine mercy to the lofty height of the pontificate so that, as God’s servant, we may provide support and assistance to God’s poor and bestow benefits upon them. Such acts befit our dignity, adorn our office, and enhance our reputation. Therefore we wish it known to all, present and future, how we granted this favor to the religious servants of God at the place in our diocese called Brombach: the persons who held two thirds of the tithes of the monastery itself and of its two nearby granges, Oberbrunn and Lengenfeld, as benefices were to redeem them and hold them forever for their own use.

The brothers gave 45 talents to the knight Crafto von Rudingsheim so that he would surrender the tithes to his lord Gernod von Roelbach. They then gave Gernod ten [talents] and a palfrey worth one talent so that he, in turn, would surrender those tithes to his lord, Mengenlan von Aschaffenburg. Likewise, they gave Mengenlan three and a half marks so that he, in turn, would surrender the aforesaid tithes to his lord, Boppo, Count von Wertheim. Boppo then surrendered them into our hands so that we might solemnly bestow them upon God and the brothers of the aforesaid place, in honor of Saint Mary, Mother of God, on the relics of the saints at Brombach, and confirm them to be held forever. Therefore, in view of divine reward, we ourselves transferred the aforesaid tithes upon the relics and confirmed this act under anathema and by the authority of our office, through this charter of privilege and the impression of our seal.

To ensure that this pious act remains more firmly in force among our successors, we received in exchange from the religious men a certain manor which they had bought from Lutold von Gundelsheim, on the condition that every year, on the Feast of the Annunciation of the Blessed Mary, they offer at the high altar of the Church of Saint Kilian two candles weighing one pound each, as a gift, and thereby make the exchange known to all. If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the terms of this charter, should in future rashly oppose it or presume in any way to disturb, molest, or trouble those brothers in the collection of the aforesaid tithes, let that person be deprived of the fellowship of all Christians, barred from receiving the sacred body and blood of the Lord, and condemned in the world to come to the eternal torments of hell with the devil and his companions.

Witnesses: clergy—Persius, dean of the cathedral; Godefridus, cantor; Albertus, custodian; Godefridus, scholasticus; Eberhard von Marmore; Godefridus, porter; Beringerus von Cimbre; Wuherus, provost of Saint John the Baptist; Albertus, dean of the same church; Tieno, deacon; Herold, abbot of Saint Burkhard; Babinold, abbot of Zell. Laymen: the Emperor’s sons Otto and Conrad; Count Boppo von Wertheim; Sigebodo von Zimmern and his son Heinrich; Berenger von Phasich; Tragebodo von Engilstat; Berenger von Gamenburg; Otto von Eschenhausen. Ministerials: Engelhard von Biebelrieth; Ruger and Otto von Homburg; Hermann, chamberlain; Gerhard von Bastheim; Heinrich von Gollach; Boto and Heinrich, schultheiss, of Würzburg; Eggehardus Granius; Heroldus; Arnoldus; Wuhardus; Adelhur von Würzburg; and many others. Done in the year of the Lord 1180, during the reign of Emperor Frederick, when Boppo was prefect of the city, in the thirteenth indiction.
